front: How do you start a dashboard and put a sheet on it?
back: Click the New Dashboard icon at the bottom of the workbook. Then drag views from the Sheets list at the left onto the dashboard at the right.

front: Dashboard objects
back: Items you add from the Objects section besides sheets: Horizontal and Vertical layout containers, Text, Image, Web Page, Blank (spacing) and Navigation.

front: Navigation object
back: A dashboard object that lets the audience move from one dashboard to another, or to other sheets or stories.

front: Worksheet, dashboard, story: what is each?
back: A worksheet holds one view. A dashboard arranges several worksheets (plus text, images and controls) on one screen. A story is a sequence of sheets or dashboards, one per story point.

front: How do you make one filter card filter every sheet on a dashboard?
back: Open the card menu and choose Apply to Worksheets > Selected worksheets, then click All on dashboard.

front: Use as Filter
back: A button in the upper corner of a dashboard sheet. It makes the selected marks filter the other sheets on the dashboard. It is a one-click filter action.

front: Data highlighter
back: Lets viewers search for data points with keywords or pick from a drop-down list. Matching marks stand out and the rest fade. It also appears on dashboards and stories.

front: How do you edit what a tooltip shows?
back: On the Marks card, select Tooltip. Use the Insert menu at the top of the dialog box to add dynamic text such as field values.

front: How do you put a whole sheet inside a tooltip?
back: Use a Viz in Tooltip: in the Tooltip Editor, choose Insert > Sheets and pick the sheet.

front: Show/Hide button
back: Added from the pop-up menu in the upper corner of a dashboard object (Add Show/Hide Button). For example, it can fold away a panel of filters.

front: Where do you create dashboard actions?
back: On a dashboard, select Dashboard > Actions, then Add Action and choose the type.

front: Which action types can you add under Dashboard > Actions?
back: Filter, Highlight, Go to URL, Go to Sheet, Change Parameter and Change Set Values.

front: Filter action vs. highlight action
back: A filter action removes marks from the target sheets. A highlight action keeps all marks and dims the others. If other values must stay visible, use highlight.

front: What can "Run action on" be set to?
back: Hover, Select (optionally single-select only) or Menu, which is a link in the tooltip.

front: What happens when a filter action selection is cleared?
back: You choose: Leave the filter, Show all values or Exclude all values. Parameter actions offer Keep current value or Set value to.

front: How do you write a URL action link that uses a field value?
back: Put the field name in angle brackets, as in `https://example.com/title?id=<Title ID>`. The field must be used in the view; Detail is enough.

front: Is Use as Filter the same as a dashboard action?
back: Use as Filter creates a filter action from that sheet to the others. Custom behaviour (hover, menu, targets, clearing) is set under Dashboard > Actions.

front: Tiled vs. floating items
back: Tiled items do not overlap and form a single-layer grid. Floating items can be layered over other objects. Hold Shift while dragging to float an item.

front: Horizontal vs. vertical layout container
back: A horizontal container resizes the width of the views and objects it holds. A vertical container adjusts height.

front: Which dashboard sizes exist, and which is the default?
back: Fixed size (the default, can pick a preset such as Desktop Browser), Range (between a minimum and a maximum) and Automatic (fills the window).

front: How do you add a phone or tablet layout to a dashboard?
back: On the Dashboard tab, click Device Preview, pick a device type, then click Add Layout (for example Add Tablet Layout). Device layouts appear under Default.

front: What must you check when publishing a dashboard with device layouts?
back: Make sure the Show sheets as tabs check box is cleared, so the device layouts are used.

front: How do you create a story?
back: Click the New Story tab. Drag a sheet or dashboard into the story, then click Add a caption to summarize the story point.

front: Blank vs. Duplicate when adding a story point
back: Blank starts a fresh story point. Duplicate copies the current one so you can change it, for example with a filter or highlight.

front: You changed a filter in a story point. How do you keep it?
back: Click Update on the story toolbar above the navigator box. Save as New keeps both versions.

front: Story point vs. dashboard
back: A dashboard shows several sheets at once. A story shows one sheet or dashboard per story point, in sequence, with captions.
